![What's new in Hamstr 0.7.1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mailo037/Hamstr/v0.7.1/docs/images/releases/v0.7.1.png)

Hamstr 0.7.1 makes the desktop app feel installed: it lives in the tray, starts with your computer if you like, and comes as a proper setup on Windows.

- **Tray.** Closing the window leaves Hamstr in the tray (Windows notification area, macOS menu bar), so downloads keep going and your phone can still send it links. A link that arrives shows a short notice. Click the icon to open Hamstr again; its menu also stashes a copied link or quits. Settings › About › *Keep running in the tray* switches it off.
- **Start with this computer** (Settings › About): Hamstr starts in the tray when you sign in.
- **Windows:** a setup `.exe` instead of the `.msi`. It puts Hamstr in the Start menu and the Apps list, where it shows as "Hamstr". There's also a portable `.zip` to unpack and run without installing.
- **Linux:** the `.deb` is in the release again (0.7.0's Linux build failed) and adds Hamstr to the app menu.
- One `SHA256SUMS.txt` now covers every file of the release.
- Fixes: a paused or queued download showed "64 %%" instead of "64 %".

Coming from 0.7.0 on Windows: its updater looks for an `.msi`, so it opens this page instead. Run the setup `.exe` once; it installs over the old version.

Signed APKs are available for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 and all ABIs together. The desktop installers aren't signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper ask before the first start. Verify every file against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
